source.title: SUPER-ADAM: Faster and Universal Framework of Adaptive Gradients
source.authors: Fei-Hu Huang; Junyi Li; Heng Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary materials are present; some experimental results are shown only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on image and language-modeling tasks and reports train and test performance, using a different optimizer framework than the version's cited comparisons.
record.gate_note: The experiments compare SUPER-ADAM with SGD and adaptive optimizers, but the supplied text does not give the plotted optimizer-specific test values or describe how SGD compares with Adam. Reported comparisons of SUPER-ADAM with other optimizers do not establish V4's stated adaptive-optimizer versus SGD pattern.
record.test_reason: The study compares SGD and adaptive optimizers using training and held-out performance on image classification and language modeling. These experiments bear on V4, but the supplied text omits the plotted SGD-versus-Adam outcomes, preventing a directional verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: the authors report superior performance for SUPER-ADAM, especially with τ = 1, and comparable performance to Adam-type methods with τ = 0. Their overall conclusion also emphasizes a universal adaptive-gradient framework and nonconvex convergence guarantees.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a new adaptive-gradient framework with other optimizers on image and language tasks; does not reproduce the cited adaptive-optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, and SUPER-ADAM setting τ (1 versus 0) are varied; the text describes different relative performance by τ.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that SUPER-ADAM with τ = 1 outperforms the compared optimizers, whereas τ = 0 performs comparably to Adam-type methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SUPER-ADAM's relative training and held-out performance depends on its gradient-estimator setting.

record.peer_reviewed: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021)
record.problems: Optimizer-specific test values are presented in figures without numerical values or a textual account of the SGD-versus-Adam comparison relevant to V4.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the text does not state optimizer-specific held-out values or comparisons sufficient to map the reported plots to the V4 conditions.

untested.parts: Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

The limited-tuning condition is not isolated: image experiments search learning rates and other hyperparameters. No controlled comparison of narrow versus broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD is reported. SGD-versus-Adam held-out outcomes are tested but unreadable in the supplied text.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions; language-model dropout is fixed at 0.5.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps. The adaptive matrix's condition number measures a different construct.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to correct. Figures 1–3, 5–7 contain relevant optimizer comparisons, but their curves and values are absent from the supplied text. Their omission is already declared in rows_left_out, so no additional missing entry is warranted. SUPER-ADAM's reported superiority does not establish the relative ordering of SGD and Adam. Introductory statements that adaptive methods generalize worse than SGD cite prior work and supply no independent evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Network width relative to the interpolation threshold.
The text reports optimizer comparisons, but does not state the SGD-versus-Adam held-out outcomes needed to assess this version.
Large versus small batch size and its effect under fixed epoch budgets.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
